en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eleventh Chapter
The Discourse on the Power of Psychic Potency:
"Could one endowed with the power of psychic potency remain for an eon?
"Yes."
Is that life-span made of psychic power, is that destiny made of psychic power, is that acquisition of a personal existence made of psychic power?
One should not say so… [as before] … Could one endowed with the power of psychic power remain for an eon?
“Yes,” you say.
“Would it remain for a past eon? Would it remain for a future eon?
You must not say so …pe…
"Is it possible that one endowed with the power of psychic success (iddhi) might remain for an eon?
"Yes.
"Would he then remain for two eons, three eons, or four eons?"
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “One endowed with the power of psychic success (iddhi) could remain for an eon”? Yes.
"If life exists and there is a remainder of life, would he remain? Or if life does not exist and there is no remainder of life, would he remain?
"If life exists and there is a remainder of life, he would remain.
"If, indeed, when life exists and there is a remainder of life he would remain, then surely it should not be said—"
“Endowed with the power of psychic potency, one might remain for an eon.
[If this were so,] would it mean that one remains while there is no life-force remaining, that one remains dead, or that one remains having passed away?
One should certainly not say such a thing …pe… .
"One endowed with the power of psychic potency might remain for an eon"?—
Yes. "It is possible to sustain through psychic potency the thought, 'Let the arisen contact not cease'"?— No.
It should not be said thus … [and so on] … feeling that has arisen … perception that has arisen … [and so on].
Arisen volition …pe… arisen consciousness … arisen faith …
arisen energy … arisen mindfulness … arisen concentration … [and so on] …
"Is it possible, by means of psychic power (*iddhi*), to sustain wisdom that has arisen so that it does not cease?
"One should not say so. ...
"Could one endowed with the power of psychic power remain for an eon (*kappa*)?"...
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Is it possible, by means of psychic power (iddhi), to exert [the will] such that ‘form (rūpa) shall be permanent’?
“It should not be said so,” and so forth.
Feeling … perception … volitional formations …
Is it possible, by means of psychic power (*iddhi*), to sustain consciousness with the thought, "Let consciousness be permanent"?
One should not say so... [etc.
...Could one endowed with the power of psychic power remain for an eon (*kappa*)?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is it possible, by means of psychic power (*iddhi*), to exert control so that beings subject to birth do not undergo birth?
One should not say so … [and so on] …
"Is it possible, by means of psychic power, to hold back beings subject to aging with the thought, 'May they not age'...
beings subject to illness with the thought, 'May they not fall ill'...
or beings subject to death with the thought, 'May they not die'?"
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said:
“One endowed with the power of psychic potency could remain for an eon”?
“Yes, [it would].
“Is it not said by the Blessed One:

‘Ānanda, whoever has developed, cultivated, made a vehicle of, made a foundation of, established, consolidated, and properly undertaken the four bases of psychic power, he could, if he so desired, remain for an eon or for the remainder of an eon’?”
Is that indeed the Sutta? Yes.
Then, in that case, one endowed with the power of psychic potency (iddhi-bala) could remain for an eon (kappa).
"Could one endowed with the power of psychic potency remain for an eon?
"Yes.
"Has it not been said by the Blessed One:"
“Bhikkhus, for four things there is no guarantor whatsoever—whether a recluse, a brahmin, a deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone else in the world.
For which four?
‘May that which is subject to aging not age’—for this there is no guarantor whatsoever, whether a recluse, a brahmin, a deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone else in the world.”
‘May I, who am subject to illness, not fall ill’ …pe… ‘May I,
who am subject to death, not die’ …pe… and as for those evil,
defiled actions conducive to renewed existence and fraught with danger that were previously committed—
“Resulting in suffering in the future, leading to birth, aging, and death—their ripening must not come to pass:
there is no guarantor for this, whether ascetic or brahmin, deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone else in the world.
Indeed, monks, for these four things there is no guarantor whatsoever in the world, whether ascetic, brahmin, deva, Māra, Brahmā, or anyone else.”
Is that indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it should not be said—
“Endowed with the power of psychic potency, one might remain for an eon.
The Discussion on the Power of Psychic Potency is finished.
